Existing common isn't vaporized by a 90% conversion.

The US deficit is surging despite low unemployment.

The cumulative US fiscal deficit since 2020 has surged to a massive $14.18 trillion.

Meanwhile, the 7-year average unemployment rate has fallen -0.4 percentage points, to 4.7% over the same period.

In the first 11 months of FY2026 alone, the US deficit totaled $1.97 trillion, the 3rd-largest for this period of the year in history.

When the economy is strong and unemployment is low, the government would typically keep fiscal deficits lower, reserving large-scale fiscal support for periods of economic weakness.

This time, however, the deficit is running at historically high levels despite stable unemployment.

This comes as elevated government spending and rising interest costs are keeping the deficit exceptionally large even without a recession.

Massive deficits have become a permanent feature of the US economy.

.@DavidSacks on the time Peter Thiel saved PayPal:

“I really liked working with him. When he hired me, he basically told me, ‘I need people here who I can scream at.’”

“I think what he meant by that was, I need people who can scream at me too. People who will be honest, and you don't even have to worry about hurting people's feelings.”

“He's a great contrarian thinker. I think that was the unique thing he brought—he'd always come up with these strategic insights that everybody else had just kind of missed.”

“Right before the dot-com crash in early 2000, Peter was raising a financing round for us and we got something like $200M in commitments to invest at a $500 million pre-money valuation. PayPal had no revenue, no profits, and not even really a business model.”

“This is the peak of the dot-com euphoria. Everyone in the company was saying, ‘That's too cheap, this is a bad deal, we can't do this.’”

“He's like, ‘Take it.’”

“We got the deal done the Friday before Black Monday. If we had waited just one more day—game over. There would not have been a PayPal.”

“He was the only one who really saw the bubble for what it was.”

“If it wasn't for his contrarian thinking, we would have been swept away with the rest of the bubble companies.”
